knowledge_units.context_summary: The study presents a workflow to identify viable crystal structures for cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO) by filtering overlapping lithium atoms and symmetry duplicates before applying machine learning for energetic ordering. The authors note that c-LLZO has the best interfacial stability against metallic lithium among popular solid electrolytes but is not stable at room temperature without dopants. The methodology aims to resolve disagreements in the literature regarding the ground state configuration and Li site occupancy of c-LLZO.

attributes.stability: not stable at room temperature without substitutional dopants
attributes.interfacial_stability: best among popular fast ion conducting solid electrolytes against metallic Li

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study addresses the lack of consensus on the lithium occupancy in cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO) by generating and ranking all possible site occupancies. A brute-force approach is deemed unviable due to the vast number of combinations, so a geometric constraint of a minimum Li-Li distance of 1.7 Å is applied to eliminate overlapping atoms. This constraint limits the feasible 24d:96h site ratios, specifically restricting the 96h sites to a maximum occupancy of 48 due to their paired geometry.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study describes a workflow to generate and filter crystal structures for cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 by enforcing minimum Li-Li distances and removing symmetry duplicates. Local sensitive hashing is used to efficiently identify unique structures, reducing the dataset to approximately 2 million unique conformations. DFT calculations on subsets of these structures are used to train a multiple linear regression model for energetic ordering.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study performed 1235 single-point DFT calculations using the ONETEP code to train a multiple linear regression model for predicting c-LLZO energies. The model achieved a correlation of 0.9996 on the test set, identifying four low-energy structures with an 8:48 24d:96h ratio within 0.026 eV of the ground state.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The authors developed a fast evaluation procedure to generate and energetically order crystallographically predicted structures for crystals with partially occupied sites. They used this method to demonstrate that many existing experimental and theoretical structures for cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO) are physically infeasible due to atomic overlap. The study aims to improve accuracy and reproducibility in future computational research on this solid electrolyte.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates the COMPASSIII forcefield for ordering c-LLZO structures, finding it insufficient for the full configuration space due to energy separation issues. ONETEP DFT calculations were performed using PBE functional and 830 eV cutoff to validate the method. A Li-dimer analysis identified an optimal inter-atomic distance of approximately 2.7 Å.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzed 2 million symmetry-unique c-LLZO structures, finding a slight correlation between higher symmetry and lower energy, though symmetry was excluded from the final MLR model due to negligible impact. Geometry optimization of 20 structures revealed that Li atoms moving from their original sites correlates with lower energy, while site transitions (e.g., 96h to 24d) were rare and did not significantly correlate with energy.
